title: The Man Who Stole the Dish of Gold

keywords: the man who stole the dish of gold
full_text:
In Cairo lived an impoverished porter named Mansur who worked from dawn until dusk, yet could barely earn enough copper to buy bread for his sick wife and young daughter. One evening, after delivering a heavy load of cedar beams to the mansion of a wealthy nobleman, he found himself alone in a banquet hall.

Upon a silver side-table lay a magnificent golden dish studded with turquoises, left behind by careless servants. Mansur looked at the gleaming gold. Thoughts of his weeping wife and hungry child rushed into his mind. In a moment of overwhelming weakness, he slipped the heavy golden dish beneath his rough cloak and fled into the night.

Returning home, he hid the dish beneath the floorboards. But sleep deserted him completely. Every rustle of the wind sounded like the guards knocking at the gate. When he looked at his daughter eating bread bought with pawning a piece of his old coat, he thought: 'Shall I feed my pure child on the proceeds of theft?'

Conscience struck him with such agony that before dawn, Mansur dug up the golden dish, walked back to the grand mansion, and threw himself at the nobleman’s feet.

'My lord,' wept Mansur, 'hunger tempted me, and I took this golden dish last night. But my father’s memory and my own soul could not bear the weight of stolen gold. Here is your treasure. Hang me or beat me as the law decrees, but let my family know I returned it with clean hands.'

The nobleman looked at the heavy gold, and then at the shivering, honest porter. His heart was touched with deep admiration.

'Rise, brother,' said the nobleman gently. 'He who steals in hunger and returns his prize in tears is no criminal, but a man of pure honor tested by adversity. Keep the golden dish as a gift from my household, and come tomorrow to be the chief steward of my storehouses.' Mansur’s honesty transformed his despair into a lifetime of honorable abundance.
moral: Honesty and returning what was taken unjustly brings lasting peace and unexpected abundance.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Man Who Stole the Dish of Gold"?
options: True wealth lies in contentment and honesty; greed leads to ruin.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
